blocks.text: Condo buildings in Burnaby Lake

MLS listing classification uses the name "Burnaby Lake" differently: as a Burnaby South band around Canada Way and Rosewood Street, south of Highway 1 by Deer Lake and Robert Burnaby Park, where the current "Burnaby Lake" listings are detached houses, not condos.
Streets, schools and getting around Burnaby Lake

items.t: The sub-area wraps Burnaby Lake Regional Park. The lake and park themselves are not residential land: the park is a Metro Vancouver regional park of 360 acres, managed by Metro Vancouver since 1978, with a 25-year City/Metro Vancouver lease signed. No condo can front the lake because the shoreline is parkland.

West and north-west side: the Sperling and Kensington streets below Lougheed Highway. East side: Government Road and Beaverbrook, toward Lougheed Town Centre. Lougheed Highway is the northern anchor road.
Recreation anchors: the Burnaby Lake Sports Complex and the Bill Copeland Sports Centre at 3676 Kensington Avenue (2,000 seats).
Transit anchor: Sperling–Burnaby Lake Station, served by routes 110, 134 and 144.
Schools beside the edges: Sperling Elementary (2200 Sperling Avenue), École Seaforth (7881 Government Road) and Burnaby Central Secondary (6011 Deer Lake Parkway).
Where condo stock concentrates: nowhere verified —. The residential streets in both the park-wrap geography and the MLS-named southern band are detached-house streets.

blocks.text: Good to know about Burnaby Lake

items.t: The park has been regionally run for almost five decades. Metro Vancouver has managed Burnaby Lake Regional Park since 1978, and a 25-year City/Metro Vancouver lease is signed — the greenbelt around the lake is a settled long-term arrangement, not land awaiting development.

The arena beside the lake seats 2,000. The Bill Copeland Sports Centre at 3676 Kensington Avenue, part of the Burnaby Lake Sports Complex, is a 2,000-seat facility — event-night traffic on Kensington Avenue is a real factor for the streets west of the park.
A 33% sales ratio here means one sale.
The one townhome complex is marketed under a different lake's name.
Jared's own sold history in this sub-area is not verified.

Streets, schools and getting around Burnaby Lake

items.t: "Burnaby Lake" is the GVR board sub-area name as used in the SnapStats GVR report for Burnaby; the sub-area wraps Burnaby Lake Regional Park in central-east Burnaby — the residential streets on the lake's edges (the Sperling and Kensington side to the west and north-west, the Government Road and Beaverbrook side to the east) around a large regional park and lake that are not themselves residential land.
Where the townhouse stock concentrates: in the park-wrap geography, nowhere verified — the residential streets are detached-house streets.

Park and recreation anchors: Burnaby Lake Regional Park is a 360-acre Metro Vancouver regional park, managed by Metro Vancouver since 1978 under a 25-year City/Metro Vancouver lease; the Burnaby Lake Sports Complex (5 lit artificial turf fields, 17 tennis courts in the City's listings) and the Bill Copeland Sports Centre, 3676 Kensington Avenue (2,000 seats), sit at the Kensington/Sperling side.

Transit anchor: Sperling–Burnaby Lake Station (Millennium Line) at Sperling Avenue and Lougheed Highway, at the sub-area's north-west side — you can walk into the park directly from the station — with bus routes 110, 134 and 144 connecting there.

Schools beside the edges: School District 41 (Burnaby) runs 41 elementary and 8 secondary schools with no middle tier (K–7 / 8–12), and catchments are address-based through the SD41 locator. Schools on the Province's list beside the sub-area include Sperling Elementary (K–7), 2200 Sperling Ave, École Seaforth Elementary (K–7), 7881 Government Rd, and Burnaby Central Secondary (8–12), 6011 Deer Lake Parkway; no SD41 school sits on the park lands.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Burnaby Lake

items.t: Lake-edge checks: the lake shore is low, marshy protected wildlife habitat — Metro Vancouver's park materials describe the shoreline habitat the trails and boardwalks are built around — so lake-edge and creek-edge lots need parcel-level flood, habitat and watercourse-setback checks; a floodplain designation for the sub-area's residential streets was not confirmed in the sources read.

Burnaby property taxes and utilities: 2026 property taxes were due Friday, July 3, 2026, with a 5% penalty after the July due date and a further 5% penalty after the September due date; Council approved a 2.9% increase (about $61 on the average home). The 2026 residential utility notice covers annual water, annual sewer use and a garbage toter fee; the detached single-family water charge is $652.33, with a 5% discount if paid by the due date.

blocks.text: Good to know about Burnaby Lake

items.t: The park has been regionally run for almost five decades (researched Nov 1, 2026). Metro Vancouver has managed Burnaby Lake Regional Park since 1978, and the City and Metro Vancouver have signed a 25-year lease agreement securing that management, with a Park Management Plan to be developed with the City within five years — the greenbelt around the lake is a settled long-term arrangement, not land awaiting development.
The one townhome complex is marketed under a different lake's name (checked Nov 1, 2026).
A 33% sales ratio here means one sale (as of September 2026). Quoting the percentage without the counts misleads in both directions.

The arena beside the lake seats 2,000 (researched Nov 1, 2026). The Bill Copeland Sports Centre at 3676 Kensington Avenue, part of the Burnaby Lake Sports Complex, is a 2,000-seat venue (1,984 permanent seats) used for hockey, lacrosse, events and concerts — event-night traffic on Kensington Avenue is a real factor for the streets west of the park, and City programs there continue during construction of the new recreation complex.

The realistic future strata route here is SSMUH, not a project (researched Nov 1, 2026). Under Burnaby's Zoning Bylaw 2026 (No. 14815) R1 rules, a house lot can hold 3 units (lots up to 280 m²), 4 units (larger lots) or 6 units (lots of at least 281 m² within 400 m of a frequent-transit stop), and multi-unit lots may be stratified — small strata product on these streets would arrive lot by lot, not as a named complex.
Jared's own sold history in this sub-area is not verified (researched Nov 1, 2026).
